name: decide
description: Use this to ask several questions of any type about the same state in one call, for example a route, an urgency and an escalation flag for one ticket. Returns `answers` by question id, with the `model` that answered, the `input_tokens` counted and the call's `cost` in USD. A point or box question with `max` (2 to 16) finds every match, up to that many, such as each car in a picture. Costs one request, with the state counted once. `model` is optional: leave it out for the default model, or pass `decisionnode-flash` for the faster, lower-cost tier.

additionalProperties.description: One question, exactly in the API's form.

instructions.description: The question or statement: a string, or a JSON value holding it.
instructions.title: Instructions

criteria.description: truth: {"true": ..., "false": ...}, what a yes and a no mean (optional). choice: an object of option name to description (null when the name says enough), 1 to 255 options. score: the list of levels, lowest first, 1 to 10. number, point and box: not used.
criteria.title: Criteria

min.description: number only: the lowest possible answer (default 0).

max.description: number: the highest possible answer (default 255). point and box: the most places to answer, an integer from 2 to 16; the answer then lists every match, up to that many.

step.description: number only: the grid of possible answers, 1 for whole numbers (the default), 0.5 for halves.

image.description: point and box only: the id of the image to look in (a string), needed when the request has two or more images. A reference by number ("Picture 2") goes in the instructions.

units.description: point and box only: pixels (the default): pixels of the image as sent. normalized: fractions of the width and the height, from 0 to 1.

questions.description: Question id to question, exactly as the API takes it: {type, instructions, criteria}; for a number {type, instructions, min, max, step}; for a point or a box {type, instructions, image, units}, which needs at least one image. Ids are yours and come back as the answer keys.

state.description: What to judge: a string, or any JSON value (an object with named fields works well). The model sees only this, the question and any images. Leave it out for a question that stands on its own.
state.title: State

id.description: Unique within the request; a short, meaningful name (`receipt`, not `2`). The model sees the image as `Picture <n> (<id>):`, so the instructions can refer to it by this id in backticks (recommended) or by its number.

url.description: An https URL the API fetches.

path.description: A file on the user's machine. Local server only; the hosted server refuses it.

images.description: Up to 16 images every question can see, within the model's token limit, each with a short, meaningful id (`receipt`, not `2`). The instructions refer to an image by its id in backticks (recommended) or by its number from 1 in this order ("image 2", "Picture 2"). Each is {id, url} with an https URL, {id, data, media_type} with base64 data, or, on the local server only, {id, path} for a file on the user's machine. On the hosted server the base64 data of one call is limited to about 3 MiB in total; send larger images by https url.

model.description: The model id. Leave it out for the default, `decisionnode-moe`; `decisionnode-flash` is the faster, lower-cost tier. The `models` tool lists the ids your key may use.

answers.description: Answers by question id. Each has `type` and that type's fields: `truth`; `choice`, `confidence`, `probabilities`; `score`, `confidence`, `legend`, `probabilities`; `number`, `expected`, `confidence`, `probabilities`; or, for a point or a box, `x` and `y` or `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, with `present`, `confidence`, `image`, `width`, `height`. A point or box asked with `max` answers `count`, `present`, `complete` (the probability that nothing was left out) and `points` or `boxes`, each with its own `confidence`, left to right, then `image`, `width` and `height`.

cost.description: What the call cost, as the API booked it, in USD: `usd` (the amount booked), split into `model_usd` and `boosters_usd`, and `free_tier` (true when the free tier covered the model's part).

safety.description: Present only when the safety check flagged a category for this key: each category's probability and the `flagged` categories.
